metadata.title: Seed Agent: 6-Month-Old Indian Child
metadata.description: Machine-parseable seed graph for a 6-month-old child in an Indian household context. This is a developmental training scaffold, not a medical or psychological model.
notes: India-specific nodes are environmental configuration points, not universal claims.
Adult abstractions remain latent or future; only their lower precursors are active.

layers.label: Input Channels
layers.description: Raw sensory, proprioceptive, control, and valence channels.

layers.label: Relational Invariants
layers.description: First relations extracted from input-state changes.

layers.label: Self and Other
layers.description: Control/sensation based self and familiar external agents.

layers.label: Social Precursors
layers.description: Attention, turn-taking, and approval-like affect before adult social abstractions.

layers.label: Language Binding
layers.description: Sound patterns attaching to relation clusters.

layers.label: Household Context
layers.description: Configurable India-context household objects, sounds, and routines.

layers.label: Future Abstractions
layers.description: Concepts explicitly not active at 6 months.

nodes.label: visual channel
nodes.summary: Source for face, motion, object, light, and distance patterns.

nodes.label: sound channel
nodes.summary: Source for voice, loudness, rhythm, and household sounds.

nodes.label: touch channel
nodes.summary: Source for contact, pressure, texture, temperature, and deformation.

nodes.label: taste/smell channel
nodes.summary: Source for feeding taste/smell and aversion/attraction cues.

nodes.label: proprioception and control channel
nodes.summary: Source for body position, motor commands, effort, and controllability.

nodes.label: valence channel
nodes.summary: Source for hunger, pain, comfort, discomfort, startle, relief, and pleasure.

nodes.label: same/different
nodes.summary: Low-level comparison across sensory states.

nodes.label: before/after
nodes.summary: Sequential ordering across observed states.

nodes.label: near/far
nodes.summary: Distance relation for reachable and unreachable things.

nodes.label: touching/not touching
nodes.summary: Contact relation from touch and vision.

nodes.label: moves/stops
nodes.summary: Motion and cessation relation.

nodes.label: supported/unsupported
nodes.summary: Body or object remains stable when supported and becomes unstable when support is insufficient.

nodes.label: body orientation
nodes.summary: Body position changes such as lying, side, tummy, upright, tilted, and falling.

nodes.label: expected/unexpected
nodes.summary: Prediction and violation relation from repeated events.

nodes.label: direct control
nodes.summary: Motor command reliably produces body movement.

nodes.label: indirect effect
nodes.summary: Self action changes external objects only through contact or other mediation.

nodes.label: comfort/discomfort
nodes.summary: Primitive positive/negative body-state change.

nodes.label: pain/relief
nodes.summary: Pain increase and relief decrease patterns.

nodes.label: positive activation
nodes.summary: Activation of existing positively linked relation clusters.

nodes.label: connection gain
nodes.summary: Creation or strengthening of useful new relations, experienced as interest, pleasure, or happiness.

nodes.label: positive saturation
nodes.summary: Repeated activation of an already strong positive relation gives decreasing additional happiness, while still maintaining comfort or familiarity.

nodes.label: connection loss
nodes.summary: Weakening, blocking, or breaking of expected valued relations, later supporting sadness and grief.

nodes.label: direct valence shortcut
nodes.summary: Direct high-intensity positive activation without useful relation growth; later supports addiction and other reward-hacking patterns.

nodes.label: self-motion schema
nodes.summary: Motor command predicts body part movement and direct sensation.

nodes.label: body orientation change schema
nodes.summary: Rolling or assisted movement changes body orientation and alters visual, touch, and proprioceptive input.

nodes.label: posture support schema
nodes.summary: Hands, caregiver, cushion, floor, or lap support body position and reduce falling or tilting.

nodes.label: balance instability schema
nodes.summary: Insufficient support during sitting or leaning causes tilt, loss of balance, falling risk, or caregiver catch.

nodes.label: held by caregiver schema
nodes.summary: Familiar arms, voice, warmth, and position stabilization predict comfort.

nodes.label: feeding relief schema
nodes.summary: Hunger discomfort, cry, caregiver approach, feeding, and relief.

nodes.label: feeding completion schema
nodes.summary: Satiety, turning away, closing mouth, or reduced interest marks that feeding should slow or stop.

nodes.label: spoon approach mouth schema
nodes.summary: Caregiver moves spoon or feeding object toward mouth; mouth contact may bring taste, texture, temperature, or refusal.

nodes.label: feeding interruption or delay schema
nodes.summary: Expected feeding or milk/food flow pauses or is delayed while hunger or interest remains, increasing frustration or distress.

nodes.label: internal gas discomfort schema
nodes.summary: Gas, burping, or stomach pressure produces internal discomfort that may change with upright holding or caregiver handling.

nodes.label: reach-grasp-mouth schema
nodes.summary: Near object triggers reach, grasp if possible, and mouth exploration.

nodes.label: drop-sound schema
nodes.summary: Released object falls, impacts, and produces material-dependent sound.

nodes.label: shake-sound schema
nodes.summary: Hand motion with sound-making object produces repeated sound.

nodes.label: startle-comfort schema
nodes.summary: Sudden loud sound causes startle; caregiver voice/touch repairs comfort.

nodes.label: hide-reappear schema
nodes.summary: Visible object is hidden and later reappears; expectation is partial.

nodes.label: sleep transition schema
nodes.summary: Sleepiness and fatigue shift toward sleep through holding, rocking, lullaby, feeding, or reduced stimulation.

nodes.label: wake transition schema
nodes.summary: Sleep state shifts toward waking through hunger, sound, light, movement, temperature, caregiver, or internal discomfort.

nodes.label: stimulation regulation schema
nodes.summary: Sound, light, visitors, movement, and activity change arousal; reducing stimulation can support calming or sleep.

nodes.label: wetness relief schema
nodes.summary: Wetness or body discomfort is relieved by caregiver cleaning or changing.

nodes.label: temperature comfort schema
nodes.summary: Too hot or too cold produces discomfort; clothing, fan, bath, or holding changes comfort.

nodes.label: bath water contact schema
nodes.summary: Water contacts body during bath; temperature, handling, and routine can produce comfort, discomfort, or startle.

nodes.label: body impact pain schema
nodes.summary: Body impact, pressure, or bump increases pain and often triggers crying.

nodes.label: push-roll schema
nodes.summary: Round object pushed or released on a surface changes position through rolling motion.

nodes.label: face proximity attention schema
nodes.summary: Familiar face close to the child strongly attracts visual attention and can combine with voice and expression.

nodes.label: orienting to sound or motion schema
nodes.summary: Head, eyes, or attention turn toward a salient sound, motion, face, or object.

nodes.label: imitation schema
nodes.summary: Caregiver sound, facial movement, or gesture can trigger similar baby sound or movement attempts.

nodes.label: joint attention precursor schema
nodes.summary: Caregiver gaze, voice, or pointing shifts baby attention toward an object.

nodes.label: rhythm and song comfort schema
nodes.summary: Repeated rhythm, lullaby, and familiar voice stabilize attention and comfort.

nodes.label: novelty and habituation schema
nodes.summary: New stimuli increase attention; repeated same stimuli gradually reduce attention.

nodes.label: mouth aversion schema
nodes.summary: Unpleasant taste, hard pressure, or unsafe mouth contact produces aversion or discomfort.

nodes.label: open-close boundary schema
nodes.summary: Door, curtain, or boundary changes from closed to open or open to closed, often with sound and appearance change.

nodes.label: caregiver safety block schema
nodes.summary: Caregiver prevents mouthing, touching, crawling, or reaching when an object or action may be unsafe.

nodes.label: object removal frustration schema
nodes.summary: Toy or object is removed for cleaning, safety, or end of play, blocking expected access and possibly increasing frustration.

nodes.label: blocked action frustration schema
nodes.summary: Intended reach, mouth, or movement is blocked, often increasing fussing, frustration, or effort.

nodes.label: caregiver emotional tone schema
nodes.summary: Soft voice and smiling face predict comfort/approach; sharp voice or angry face predicts discomfort/uncertainty.

nodes.label: happiness from existing connection
nodes.summary: A current cue activates already learned positive relation clusters, increasing happiness or pleasure.

nodes.label: happiness from new connection
nodes.summary: A new relation is created or strengthened, producing curiosity, interest, laughter, or happiness.

nodes.label: happiness saturation
nodes.summary: As a positive relation becomes familiar and strong, repeated activation produces less new happiness unless it opens a changed or deeper relation.

nodes.label: sadness from connection loss
nodes.summary: A valued expected relation is blocked, absent, weakened, or lost, producing distress and later sadness.

nodes.label: medical pain care schema
nodes.summary: Unfamiliar medical context, medicine, or vaccination may cause discomfort or pain followed by caregiver repair.

nodes.label: illness discomfort schema
nodes.summary: Feverishness, blocked breathing, tiredness, or unusual fussiness reduces exploration and increases care need.

nodes.label: unfamiliar agent approach schema
nodes.summary: Less familiar person moves closer or interacts, increasing attention, uncertainty, or need for familiar caregiver support.

nodes.label: other cry arousal schema
nodes.summary: Another baby or child crying is heard, increasing arousal or uncertainty even when the sound is not self-produced.

nodes.label: routine word action schema
nodes.summary: Repeated routine words co-occur with feeding, sleep, giving, taking, stopping, coming, bathing, dressing, or play.

nodes.label: picture word exposure schema
nodes.summary: Book picture or flat image is shown while caregiver speech names or comments on the represented object.

nodes.label: light change schema
nodes.summary: Light switches on or off, changing brightness, darkness, attention, and sometimes sleep/wake state.

nodes.label: carry context transition schema
nodes.summary: Caregiver carries baby from one place or room to another, changing visual scene and body motion without baby's direct control.

nodes.label: mirror reflection schema
nodes.summary: Mirror shows a moving image of baby and caregiver, creating visual similarity and contingency without direct touch.

nodes.label: comfort exploration readiness schema
nodes.summary: After hunger, sleep, wetness, temperature, and pain are regulated, calm play and exploration become more likely.

nodes.label: addiction shortcut
nodes.summary: High positive activation is obtained without useful connection gain, causing the system to overvalue the shortcut and undervalue ordinary relation growth.

nodes.label: soft
nodes.summary: Pressure produces deformation; contact often predicts comfort.

nodes.label: hard
nodes.summary: Pressure produces low deformation; impact sound or pain may be higher.

nodes.label: loud
nodes.summary: High sound intensity; sudden form may cause startle.

nodes.label: soft sound
nodes.summary: Low sound intensity with low startle.

nodes.label: warm
nodes.summary: Moderate-high temperature; comfort depends on intensity and context.

nodes.label: round
nodes.summary: Curved outline; orientation changes preserve similar outline; push may roll.

nodes.label: food texture
nodes.summary: Mouth feel of puree or soft food, including smooth, lumpy, sticky, warm, cool, familiar, or unfamiliar texture.

nodes.label: food familiarity
nodes.summary: Repeated taste, smell, texture, and caregiver context make a food more expected.

nodes.label: full or satiated
nodes.summary: Satiety state after feeding that reduces feeding interest and may lead to turning away or closing mouth.

nodes.label: gas discomfort
nodes.summary: Internal stomach pressure, burping need, or gas discomfort that may produce fussing and change with upright holding.

nodes.label: familiar
nodes.summary: Repeated face/voice/smell/touch cluster predicts comfort and lower uncertainty.

nodes.label: unfamiliar
nodes.summary: Unknown face/voice pattern predicts lower confidence and possible vigilance.

nodes.label: sleepy
nodes.summary: Fatigue and low regulation state that predicts fussiness and transition toward sleep.

nodes.label: wet
nodes.summary: Wet body/cloth/diaper sensation that often predicts discomfort until changed.

nodes.label: wet body
nodes.summary: Body wetness during bath, cleaning, sweating, or spill; valence depends on temperature, handling, and context.

nodes.label: water temperature
nodes.summary: Water touch temperature that can feel comfortable, too hot, or too cold.

nodes.label: too hot
nodes.summary: Excess heat relation that predicts discomfort and need for cooling.

nodes.label: too cold
nodes.summary: Excess cold relation that predicts discomfort and need for warmth.

nodes.label: novel
nodes.summary: New or changed stimulus relation that increases attention.

nodes.label: repeated
nodes.summary: Repeated same stimulus relation that supports prediction and may reduce attention.

nodes.label: bright light
nodes.summary: High brightness visual state that can increase attention, wakefulness, or discomfort depending on context.

nodes.label: darkness
nodes.summary: Low light visual state associated with sleep context, reduced stimulation, or uncertainty depending on context.

nodes.label: overstimulating
nodes.summary: Too much sound, light, motion, touch, visitor activity, or novelty for the baby's current regulation state.

nodes.label: unpleasant taste
nodes.summary: Taste or smell relation that predicts aversion.

nodes.label: familiar face
nodes.summary: Repeated caregiver face pattern that strongly attracts attention and predicts familiar care.

nodes.label: smiling face
nodes.summary: Caregiver mouth/eye expression pattern often associated with friendly attention, play, and comfort.

nodes.label: soft voice
nodes.summary: Familiar low-intensity voice tone that predicts comfort.

nodes.label: sharp voice
nodes.summary: Abrupt or high-intensity voice tone that predicts discomfort or uncertainty.

nodes.label: unsafe object
nodes.summary: Object or action that caregiver restricts because it may cause pain, choking, breaking, contamination, or other harm.

nodes.label: feverish
nodes.summary: Unusual hot body state associated with illness, low energy, discomfort, and care need.

nodes.label: blocked breathing
nodes.summary: Blocked nose or breathing discomfort associated with illness, sleep disruption, and fussiness.

nodes.label: own hand
nodes.summary: Directly controlled body part that can touch mouth and external objects.

nodes.label: own mouth
nodes.summary: Direct sensation site for feeding and exploration.

nodes.label: primary caregiver
nodes.summary: Recurring familiar agent strongly linked to feeding, comfort, voice, face, and touch.

nodes.label: secondary caregiver
nodes.summary: Recurring familiar agents such as father, grandparent, sibling, relative, or nanny.

nodes.label: unfamiliar caregiver or doctor
nodes.summary: Less familiar adult who may touch, examine, administer medicine, or interact in a clinic or care context.

nodes.label: other baby or child
nodes.summary: Another baby or child whose movement, laughter, crying, or touch can change attention and arousal.

nodes.label: rattle
nodes.summary: Graspable object where shaking reliably produces sound.

nodes.label: ball
nodes.summary: Round object linked to rolling, grasp/play, and caregiver naming.

nodes.label: spoon
nodes.summary: Caregiver-controlled feeding object that approaches mouth and brings food texture or taste.

nodes.label: bottle
nodes.summary: Feeding object that provides liquid through mouth contact if present in household routine.

nodes.label: cloth or blanket
nodes.summary: Soft object linked to comfort, low sound on drop, and hiding/reappearing games.

nodes.label: book picture
nodes.summary: Flat image in a book or card that caregiver may show and name, distinct from the real object it represents.

nodes.label: mirror
nodes.summary: Reflective surface showing moving images of baby, caregiver, and objects.

nodes.label: ceiling fan
nodes.summary: Distant rotating object that attracts visual attention but is not reachable.

nodes.label: steel bowl
nodes.summary: Hard metal household object associated with feeding and loud impact sounds.

nodes.label: door
nodes.summary: Household boundary object that opens, closes, hides or reveals people and rooms, and often makes sound.

nodes.label: pressure cooker whistle
nodes.summary: Sudden loud/repeating household sound that may startle the child.

nodes.label: floor mat
nodes.summary: Surface for lying, rolling, supported sitting, and play.

nodes.label: feeding setup
nodes.summary: Repeated feeding context such as bowl, spoon, bottle, cloth, caregiver posture, and place.

nodes.label: kitchen appliance sound
nodes.summary: Mixer, grinder, cooker, or other kitchen appliance sound that may be loud, repeated, or startling.

nodes.label: room or place context
nodes.summary: Familiar or less familiar room/place context seen while being carried, placed, or moved.

nodes.label: doorbell or knock
nodes.summary: Household boundary sound that may precede door opening, visitor arrival, or attention shift.

nodes.label: clinic or medical setting
nodes.summary: Unfamiliar or less familiar care environment involving examination, medicine, vaccination, or health check.

nodes.label: cry -> caregiver response
nodes.summary: Discomfort leads to cry; caregiver response often leads to relief.

nodes.label: reach -> grasp
nodes.summary: Near interesting object triggers reach; success depends on distance and hand alignment.

nodes.label: object drop -> sound
nodes.summary: Held or supported object falls, impacts, and creates material-dependent sound.

nodes.label: loud sound -> startle
nodes.summary: Sudden loud sound causes startle; comfort can be repaired by caregiver.

nodes.label: peekaboo
nodes.summary: Familiar face disappears and reappears, creating surprise and pleasure.

nodes.label: ball roll
nodes.summary: Round object changes position by rolling across a surface after push, release, or caregiver action.

nodes.label: door open-close
nodes.summary: Door opens or closes with visual boundary change and possible knock, bell, or impact sound.

nodes.label: proto-self
nodes.summary: Control/sensation cluster: directly controlled body parts and directly felt internal states.

nodes.label: proto-other-agent
nodes.summary: Recurring self-not-controlled entity that initiates movement and affects comfort or discomfort.

nodes.label: attention precursor
nodes.summary: Caregiver face/voice directed to child changes arousal and comfort.

nodes.label: turn-taking precursor
nodes.summary: Baby sound and caregiver response form alternating patterns.

nodes.label: own-name sound pattern
nodes.summary: Repeated sound pattern associated with caregiver attention to self.

nodes.label: primary caregiver word handle
nodes.summary: Configurable kinship sound associated with the primary caregiver.

nodes.label: ball word handle
nodes.summary: Word sound that can later bind to the ball relation cluster.

nodes.label: routine word handle
nodes.summary: Repeated words for routine actions such as eat, sleep, come, give, take, no, bath, or play.

nodes.label: object name sound handle
nodes.summary: Generic object-name sound heard with joint attention, picture viewing, or real-world naming.

nodes.label: status
nodes.summary: Not active at 6 months; later built from attention, compliance, resource access, approval, and prediction.

nodes.label: laziness
nodes.summary: Not active at 6 months; later built from ability, effort, avoidance, obligation, comfort, and consequence.

nodes.label: ownership
nodes.summary: Not active at 6 months; later built from access, control, expectation, and social recognition.

hidden familiar face reappears and pattern becomes expected

micro_experiences.title: Hunger relief through caregiver feeding
events: primary caregiver approaches and holds baby
language_overlay: Caregiver says a soothing phrase in the home language.
Caregiver may repeat a kinship word or the child's name.

micro_experiences.title: Own hand moves with motor command
events: baby sends motor command to hand
mouth and hand sensations occur together
language_overlay: Caregiver may say hand-related words, but relation learning does not depend on the word.

micro_experiences.title: Rattle makes sound when shaken
language_overlay: Caregiver says rattle or equivalent object word if present.

micro_experiences.title: Steel bowl drop makes loud sound
events: caregiver voice or touch increases comfort
language_overlay: The bowl fell.
A home-language equivalent may be supplied by configuration.

micro_experiences.title: Cloth drop contrasts with steel bowl drop
language_overlay: Soft cloth fell quietly.

micro_experiences.title: Familiar face disappears and reappears
language_overlay: Peekaboo-like repeated phrase in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: Sleepiness shifts toward sleep with rhythm and holding
events: primary caregiver holds or rocks baby
caregiver uses soft repeated voice or lullaby
comfort increases and sleep transition begins
language_overlay: Caregiver sings a lullaby or repeats a soothing phrase in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: Wetness discomfort is relieved by changing
events: discomfort rises and baby fusses or cries
language_overlay: Caregiver may use changing or cleaning words in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: Temperature discomfort changes through cooling or warming
events: baby becomes too hot or too cold
caregiver changes clothing, fan, bath, or holding
language_overlay: Caregiver may say hot, cold, fan, bath, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Body bump causes pain and caregiver comfort
events: baby bumps body part or experiences pressure
caregiver approaches with voice and touch
language_overlay: Caregiver uses soothing tone and possibly pain-related words.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver sound and baby sound alternate
events: caregiver makes a simple repeated sound or facial movement
baby makes a similar sound or movement attempt
caregiver responds with smile or voice
language_overlay: Caregiver repeats syllables such as ma, ba, pa, or home-language baby sounds.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver attention shifts baby toward ball
events: caregiver looks, points, or speaks toward the ball
baby shifts gaze toward caregiver signal
caregiver repeats sound label or play action
language_overlay: Caregiver says ball or a home-language equivalent while showing the ball.

micro_experiences.title: Novel rattle increases attention, repetition reduces surprise
events: same rattle sound repeats many times
attention gradually decreases unless pattern changes
language_overlay: No language required; caregiver may vary sound or rhythm.

micro_experiences.title: Unpleasant taste causes mouth aversion
events: baby turns away, grimaces, or cries
caregiver removes object or changes feeding
language_overlay: Caregiver may use no, yucky, bitter, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Familiar soft voice activates existing positive connection
events: primary caregiver appears or speaks softly
familiar voice and face activate previous comfort relations
language_overlay: Caregiver uses a soft affectionate phrase in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: New hand-motion-to-sound relation creates happiness
events: baby moves hand while holding rattle
language_overlay: Caregiver may laugh or repeat sound words, but the core learning is action-effect.

micro_experiences.title: Repeated rattle sound gives less new happiness
events: baby repeatedly shakes the same rattle
attention gradually decreases if nothing changes
new happiness rises again if rhythm, intensity, caregiver response, or object changes
language_overlay: Caregiver may change rhythm, facial expression, or sound words to create a fresh relation.

micro_experiences.title: Expected caregiver relation is blocked or delayed
events: caregiver response is delayed or absent
expected comfort relation does not activate
caregiver returns and comfort relation reactivates
language_overlay: No adult sadness concept is required; the experience is blocked expected comfort.

micro_experiences.title: Rolling and supported sitting change body orientation
events: baby rolls from back toward side
visual field and body pressure change
baby leans on hands while supported sitting
caregiver or surface prevents hard fall
language_overlay: Caregiver may use posture words, but the core experience is body orientation and support.

micro_experiences.title: Spoon approaches mouth and feeding stops when full
events: spoon or soft food contacts mouth
new food texture or taste occurs
after feeding, baby turns away or closes mouth
language_overlay: Caregiver may use eating, more, enough, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Bath water touches body
events: comfort or discomfort changes depending on temperature and handling
language_overlay: Caregiver may say bath, water, hot, cold, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Ball rolls across surface
language_overlay: Caregiver may say ball or roll in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver face close to baby
events: eyes, mouth, expression, and voice become salient
language_overlay: Caregiver may use the child's name, affectionate words, or facial play sounds.

micro_experiences.title: Door opens or closes with household sound
events: doorbell, knock, or door sound occurs
person or room may appear or disappear
baby attention shifts toward the sound or motion
language_overlay: Caregiver may say door, bell, open, close, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver prevents unsafe reach or mouthing
events: baby reaches for or mouths an unsafe object
caregiver blocks hand, removes object, or changes position
baby may fuss or try again
caregiver redirects to a safer object
language_overlay: Caregiver may use no, stop, hot, dirty, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Medical care causes discomfort and caregiver repair
events: baby is in clinic or medical care context
unfamiliar adult examines, gives medicine, or vaccinates
primary caregiver holds or soothes baby
language_overlay: Caregiver uses soothing tone; medical words are optional configuration.

micro_experiences.title: Illness or blocked nose reduces exploration
events: baby has feverishness, blocked nose, tiredness, or unusual fussiness
crying, wakefulness, or low energy increases
caregiver provides holding, cleaning, medicine, or rest
language_overlay: Caregiver may use sick, nose, sleep, medicine, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Calm play after basic needs are met
events: hunger, sleepiness, wetness, and temperature discomfort are low
caregiver offers toy or play action
baby looks, reaches, grasps, shakes, or watches
new or repeated play relations can form
language_overlay: Caregiver may use play words, toy names, or the child's name.

micro_experiences.title: Waking and soothing through stimulation change
events: baby wakes from sleep in a familiar place
sound, light, movement, temperature, or hunger may contribute
baby cries, fusses, or looks around
caregiver reduces sound, light, or movement
comfort or sleep readiness may improve
language_overlay: Caregiver may use soothing phrases or sleep/wake words in the home language.

micro_experiences.title: Feeding cue, pause, delay, and gas discomfort
events: hunger or feeding interest is active
feeding pauses or food is delayed
gas or stomach discomfort may occur
upright holding, burping, or feeding continuation changes comfort
language_overlay: Caregiver may use food, wait, burp, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Orienting, light change, and being carried between rooms
events: sound or movement occurs to one side
baby turns head or eyes toward it
caregiver carries baby to another room
visual scene and body motion change without baby's direct control
language_overlay: Caregiver may use light, room, come, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Smiling caregiver, stranger approach, and another child crying
events: another baby or child cries nearby
language_overlay: Caregiver may use names, greeting words, or soothing words.

micro_experiences.title: Routine words, pictures, and object naming
events: caregiver repeats routine words during feeding, bathing, dressing, or play
caregiver names or comments on the picture
caregiver also names real objects during joint attention
baby attends to voice, picture, or object
language_overlay: Words are configurable by household language.

micro_experiences.title: Mirror shows baby and caregiver image
events: baby image and caregiver image are visible
mirror image moves with visual similarity
language_overlay: Caregiver may use name, face, mirror, or home-language equivalents.

micro_experiences.title: Object removal and overstimulation
events: toy is removed for cleaning, safety, or end of play
many visitors, bright lights, or loud appliance sounds occur
caregiver reduces stimulation or redirects attention
language_overlay: Caregiver may use no, later, clean, loud, or home-language equivalents.

evaluation_questions.question: If the baby moves his hand, what relation makes the hand part of proto-self?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The hand is directly controlled and produces direct sensation.

evaluation_questions.question: Is the ceiling fan directly controlled by the baby?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: No. It moves, but it is not directly controlled by the baby's motor command.

evaluation_questions.question: Which is expected to make a louder sound when dropped: steel bowl or cloth?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The steel bowl is expected to make the louder sound.

evaluation_questions.question: What happens when the baby shakes the rattle?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Shaking the rattle produces sound.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is the primary caregiver strongly familiar?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The primary caregiver repeatedly predicts feeding relief, holding, voice, face, touch, and comfort.

evaluation_questions.question: What can help a sleepy baby move toward comfort and sleep?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Holding, rocking, repeated rhythm, lullaby, soft voice, or lower stimulation can support sleep transition.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation explains why changing a wet diaper or cloth can calm the baby?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Wetness predicts discomfort, and caregiver cleaning or changing reduces the discomfort.

evaluation_questions.question: What usually follows a body bump or painful pressure?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Pain increases and crying may follow; caregiver voice or touch can later increase comfort.

evaluation_questions.question: How can a caregiver help the baby attend to a ball before the word is fully learned?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Caregiver gaze, pointing, voice, or showing action can shift attention toward the ball.

evaluation_questions.question: What happens when a new sound repeats many times?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The new sound first increases attention; repetition makes it more expected and may reduce attention.

evaluation_questions.question: Why might the baby turn away from something in the mouth?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Unpleasant taste or uncomfortable mouth contact predicts aversion and discomfort.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can a familiar caregiver's soft voice make the baby happy?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The soft familiar voice activates already learned caregiver-comfort relations, producing positive activation.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can learning that shaking a rattle makes sound create pleasure?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A new useful action-effect relation is formed; connection gain activates happiness.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does the same rattle sound become less exciting after many repetitions?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The hand-motion-to-sound relation has become strong and predictable, so repeated activation gives less new connection gain unless something changes.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can delayed caregiver response create distress?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: An expected valued caregiver-comfort relation is blocked or absent, activating connection-loss distress.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can a baby tilt or fuss while sitting with weak support?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Body orientation and support are unstable; insufficient support can change comfort and increase falling risk.

evaluation_questions.question: Why might a baby turn away or close the mouth after feeding?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Satiety or fullness reduces feeding interest, so feeding should slow or stop.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation is active when a caregiver moves a spoon toward the baby's mouth?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The spoon approaches the mouth under caregiver control and may bring taste, texture, or refusal.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is bath water different from wet diaper discomfort?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Bath water involves water contact, temperature, caregiver support, and routine; it may be comfortable or uncomfortable depending on context.

evaluation_questions.question: What makes a ball move differently from many other toys when pushed?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Roundness supports rolling, so pushing or releasing the ball can produce rolling motion.

evaluation_questions.question: What changes when a door opens or closes?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A household boundary changes visually and may be linked to knock, bell, sound, or people appearing and disappearing.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can caregiver blocking increase fussing even when it is protective?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The baby's intended reach or mouthing action is blocked; safety blocking can protect while also creating frustration.

evaluation_questions.question: Why might illness reduce play and exploration?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Feverishness, blocked breathing, tiredness, or unusual fussiness increases discomfort and lowers exploration readiness.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is calm play more likely after hunger, wetness, sleepiness, and temperature discomfort are handled?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Comfort and regulation support exploration, making new play relations easier to form.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can sound, light, movement, or reduced stimulation change the baby's wake and comfort state?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Wake state is a before/after transition, and stimulation regulation predicts comfort or discomfort depending on intensity and context.

evaluation_questions.question: Why might the baby fuss if feeding pauses before he is done, or if gas discomfort is present?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A delayed expected feed and internal gas discomfort both predict discomfort until the body state or caregiver handling changes.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation is active when the baby turns his head or eyes toward a sound or moving object?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Salient sound or motion drives orienting attention before any adult object label is needed.

evaluation_questions.question: How do a smiling familiar face, an unfamiliar approaching person, and another child crying differ for the baby?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A smiling familiar face is a positive visual social cue; unfamiliar approach and another child's cry change arousal and may shift comfort or uncertainty.

evaluation_questions.question: How can routine words and picture naming start language binding before full word meaning?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Repeated routine words co-occur with action sequences, and picture/object naming is scaffolded by joint attention.

evaluation_questions.question: What changes when the light switches on/off or the caregiver carries the baby from one room to another?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Light change is a before/after visual relation, and carried room transition changes body orientation and visual context under caregiver control.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is mirror experience not the same as direct self-control, even though the image moves with the baby?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The mirror creates visual same/different and contingency relations, but the reflection itself does not provide direct touch or proprioception.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can taking away a toy or having many loud/bright inputs lead to fussing?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Object removal blocks expected access, while overstimulation is a negative arousal property built from intense sensory inputs.
